_doc: How the fighting roles look (scripts/space/hullgen.gd with_look(), scripts/view/dressing.gd). Per role id of data/enemy_tables.json roles: `hull` is laid over the hull style of the ship's faction or race: `prow` and `tail` replace the style's, `band` sets the deck widths (shares of the widest floor by deck kind; the style's own band still caps what a deck holds, so no room is dropped for the look), `jitter_w` and `jitter_c` cap the style's jitter (a symmetric people stays symmetric), and `ops` shape the staircase before the style's own ops. The corners a role op makes are locked: the style's ops (its finish: bevels, spikes, arcs) work on the rest, so a Sporeling carrier is a Sporeling ship shaped like a carrier. A rammer keeps the style's hull (its ram bow) and the plain fallback hull its bevels. Role ops: wedge and chamfer (as the style's), keep {at} (lock those corners), fins {depth, swept} (45 degree fins out of the stern corners, swept: back past the stern too), jaw {depth, w} (a clamp tooth forward of each bow corner, its tip w wide), horns {w, reach, gap} (two horns from the shoulders where the bow narrows, `reach` rows past the bow), island {w, len, side} (a block on one flank), racks {count, h, gap, depth} (square teeth on both flanks at the same rows), steps {at: tip or stern_end, n, a, b, bevel} (stepped ends). Every slope is 45 degrees. `dressing` is added to the livery's (style.dressing entries, the same shape). Roles not listed (gunboat, brawler, escort, sniper, hauler) keep the style's hull as it is.
